q: which functional language inspired the map and reduce primitives
a: Our abstraction is inspired by the map and reduce primitives present in Lisp and many other functional languages.

q: what is the primary mechanism mapreduce uses for fault tolerance
a: Like MapReduce, it relies on re-execution as a mechanism for implementing fault-tolerance.

q: what does the master launch to handle straggler machines that slow down completion
a:
6 Backup Tasks
One of the common causes that lengthens the total time taken for a MapReduce operation is a “straggler”: a machine that takes an unusually long time to complete one of the last few map or reduce tasks in the computation.

q: why does mapreduce schedule map tasks close to the data they process
a: Our locality optimization draws its inspiration from techniques such as active disks [12, 15], where computation is pushed into processing elements that are close to local disks, to reduce the amount of data sent across I/O subsystems or the network.
